sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Our Bolzano data is recent, so there is no city trend yet; the figures below are for weekdays and weekends in August and September 2026.

Central parking supply in Bolzano is changing: surface spaces are going, and an underground car park is planned. The city's mobility plan (PUMS), approved in 2022, replaced a rejected tram with electric bus lines and said the city meant to use under-used underground car parks through agreements with third parties [1][0]. The city's traffic plan for 2025–2028 includes strategic guidelines for a later detailed plan for managing on-street parking [2]. In 2022 the city announced higher on-street prices, up to €3 an hour on several central streets, with the mayor saying the aim was to limit tourist and commuter pressure [3], and downtown parking was listed at €2 an hour in 2023 [15]. The next squeeze is physical: reports in June 2026 said four construction projects starting in autumn would reduce parking supply, notably around Piazza Vittoria, where 299 surface spaces are due to go, with 70 temporary spaces planned at Piazza Tribunale and talks with private garage operators reported as having failed [6]. Commuting is a large part of demand: about 97% of the car-park spaces assigned to provincial staff in Bolzano are used by people living outside the municipality, according to a provincial reply [23].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The replacement for the surface spaces is a five-level underground car park at Piazza della Vittoria, with 390 car spaces and a 38-year concession for about €20 million of works. The city announced a provisional award to a group led by Parcheggi Italia in October 2025 [4]. In March 2026 the regional administrative court rejected a challenge to the award, and the city said construction was now targeted between late summer and early autumn 2026, later than the June start first given [5].

Elsewhere the operators have changed hands. Best in Parking opened the 550-space WaltherPark garage in 2025 [7], and the shopping gallery at WaltherPark was reported completed that October, with the first Esselunga in South Tyrol [20]. The Province's Lauben Portici garage reopened in March 2026 under APCOA, which charges €3.50 an hour with a €20 day maximum [8][9] and plans pre-booking, app payment and toll-tag access [10]. APCOA also won the tender for the garage under the Magnago-Platz for three years from January 2026; the previous operator, which is contesting the tender in court, warned that fees would rise [11]. The city planned to waterproof the Waltherplatz above the Parcheggi Italia garage for about €5.7 million, and expected the operator to share the cost [12]. The city's page points drivers to parking.bz.it for live availability [17], and the deputy mayor has said the city wants an app showing prices and free spaces [16].

Demand is firm: tourist overnight stays in the city reached about 946,000 in 2024 [21], and the Christkindlmarkt drew about 900,000 visitors in 2023 [22].

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
Prices are highest in the centre. Within 500 m of the Piazza Walther the seven we measure hold about 2,800 spaces and average 47%. Best in Parking's Piazza Walther and WaltherPark garages charge €4.50 an hour and €24 a day and stand at 39% and 30%. The cheaper ones fill more: APCOA's Lauben garage at €3.50 is at 64%, the BZ Centro shopping-centre garage, with 1,055 spaces at €2.00, at 48%, and the SEAB garage at Piazza Tribunale, at €1.50, at 52%. The small Laurin garage (90 spaces, €3.90) is at 60%.

Weekends do not empty Bolzano's garages as they do in office-heavy cities: 38% on weekdays and 38% at weekends overall. Outside the centre, use is lower. The Palasport garage, at €0.30 an hour, runs at 51%, the NOI Techpark garage at 27% on weekdays and 8% at weekends, and the 770-space Fiera garage at 8%. Price shows no clear relation with occupancy in our data.
